column1: The typical way of talking to a baby — high-pitched, exaggerated and repetitious — is a source of fascination for linguists who hope to understand how ‘baby talk’ impacts on learning.
column2: 人们对婴儿说话时，通常会抬高音调、夸大语气、反复说。这种说话方式令语言学家着迷，因为他们想弄清“婴儿语”怎样影响学习。
column8: baby talk|成人对婴儿说的话

column1: Most babies start developing their hearing while still in the womb, prompting some hopeful parents to play classical music to their pregnant bellies.
column2: 多数婴儿还在母体中时，听觉就开始发育了。这让一些满怀期待的父母对着孕肚播放古典音乐。
column4: in the womb|在母体子宫中

column1: Some research even suggests that infants are listening to adult speech as early as 10 weeks before being born, gathering the basic building blocks of their family’s native tongue.
column2: 有些研究甚至表明，早在出生前十周，婴儿就在听大人说话，开始积累家庭母语中最基本的语言要素。
column7: basic building blocks|基本组成要素

column1: Early language exposure seems to have benefits to the brain — for instance, studies suggest that babies raised in bilingual homes are better at learning how to mentally prioritize information.
column2: 早期接触语言似乎有益于大脑。比如，研究显示，在双语家庭长大的婴儿更善于学会在头脑中区分哪些信息应优先处理。
column3: Early language exposure|早期语言接触
column8: prioritize information|按优先顺序处理信息

column1: So how does the sweet if sometimes absurd sound of infant-directed speech influence a baby’s development?
column2: 那么，大人专门对婴儿说话时，那种甜美却有时显得滑稽的声音，究竟怎样影响婴儿的发展呢？
column5: infant-directed speech|专门对婴儿说的话

column1: Here are some recent studies that explore the science behind baby talk.
column2: 下面几项近期研究，探讨了婴儿语背后的科学。
column6: baby talk|成人对婴儿说的话

column1: Fathers don’t use baby talk as often or in the same ways as mothers — and that’s perfectly OK, according to a new study.
column2: 一项新研究发现，爸爸说婴儿语的频率不如妈妈高，用法也有所不同，这完全没问题。
column4: in the same ways|用相同的方式

column1: Mark VanDam of Washington State University at Spokane and colleagues equipped parents with recording devices and speech-recognition software to study the way they interacted with their youngsters during a normal day.
column2: 华盛顿州立大学斯波坎校区的马克·范达姆和同事给父母配备了录音设备和语音识别软件，研究他们在普通的一天里如何与幼儿交流。
column3: Washington State University|华盛顿州立大学

column1: ‘We found that moms do exactly what you’d expect and what’s been described many times over,’ VanDam explains.
column2: 范达姆解释说：“妈妈们的做法和你预想的完全一样，也是以往反复描述过的那样。

column1: ‘But we found that dads aren’t doing the same thing.
column2: 但我们发现，爸爸们的做法并不相同。

column1: Dads didn’t raise their pitch or fundamental frequency when they talked to kids.’
column2: 爸爸们和孩子说话时，不会抬高音高，也就是提高声音的基频。”

column1: Their role may be rooted in what is called the bridge hypothesis, which dates back to 1975.
column2: 他们的这种作用，可能可以用追溯至1975年的“桥梁假说”来解释。

column1: It suggests that fathers use less familial language to provide their children with a bridge to the kind of speech they’ll hear in public.
column2: 按这一假说，父亲会较少使用家庭成员之间那种亲昵的语言，好让孩子逐渐过渡到他们将在公共场合听到的说话方式。

column1: ‘The idea is that a kid gets to practice a certain kind of speech with mom and another kind of speech with dad, so the kid then has a wider repertoire of kinds of speech to practice,’ says VanDam.
column2: “这个想法是，孩子能和妈妈练一种说话方式，和爸爸练另一种，这样孩子就能练习更丰富多样的说话方式。”范达姆说。
column4: a certain kind of speech|某种说话方式
column7: kinds of speech|不同的说话方式

column1: Scientists from the University of Washington and the University of Connecticut collected thousands of 30-second conversations between parents and their babies, fitting 26 children with audio-recording vests that captured language and sound during a typical eight-hour day.
column2: 华盛顿大学和康涅狄格大学的科学家收集了数千段父母和婴儿间的对话，每段30秒。他们给26名儿童穿上录音背心，记录日常一天中八小时内出现的言语和声音。
column9: eight-hour day|一天中长达八小时的时段

column1: The study found that the more baby talk parents used, the more their youngsters began to babble.
column2: 研究发现，父母越常用婴儿语，孩子就越多地开始咿呀发声。
column3: the more baby talk|越常使用婴儿语

column1: And when researchers saw the same babies at age two, they found that frequent baby talk had dramatically boosted vocabulary, regardless of socioeconomic status.
column2: 等到这些婴儿两岁，研究人员再次见到他们时发现，经常听婴儿语显著扩大了他们的词汇量，孩子的社会经济地位并不影响这一点。

column1: ‘Those children who listened to a lot of baby talk were talking more than the babies that listened to more adult talk or standard speech,’ says Nairán Ramírez-Esparza of the University of Connecticut.
column2: “经常听婴儿语的孩子，说的话比那些更多听成人用语或常规话语的孩子要多。”康涅狄格大学的奈兰·拉米雷斯-埃斯帕萨说。
column4: a lot of baby talk|大量婴儿语
column6: adult talk|成人之间的说话方式

column1: ‘We also found that it really matters whether you use baby talk in a one-on-one context,’ she adds.
column2: “我们还发现，大人是不是面对面、一对一地用婴儿语和孩子说话，确实很重要。”她补充道。

column1: ‘The more parents use baby talk one-on-one, the more babies babble, and the more they babble, the more words they produce later in life.’
column2: “父母越常一对一地用婴儿语和孩子说话，孩子就越多地咿呀发声；他们咿呀得越多，日后能说出的词也越多。”

column1: Another study suggests that parents might want to pair their youngsters up so they can babble more with their own kind.
column2: 另一项研究表明，家长或许可以让婴儿两两结伴，好让他们有更多机会和同龄孩子咿呀交谈。
column5: pair their youngsters up|让孩子两两结伴
column6: their own kind|和他们一样的婴儿

column1: Researchers from McGill University and Université du Québec à Montréal found that babies seem to like listening to each other rather than to adults — which may be why baby talk is such a universal tool among parents.
column2: 麦吉尔大学和魁北克大学蒙特利尔分校的研究者发现，婴儿似乎更喜欢听其他婴儿的声音，而不是成人的声音。这也许能解释，为什么世界各地的父母都爱用婴儿语。
column4: listening to each other|彼此聆听
column6: may be why|或许解释了为何
column7: universal tool|被普遍采用的手段

column1: They played repeating vowel sounds made by a special synthesizing device that mimicked sounds made by either an adult woman or another baby.
column2: 他们播放了反复出现的元音，这些声音由一台专门的合成设备产生，模仿的是成年女性或另一名婴儿的声音。
column3: repeating vowel sounds|反复播放的元音

column1: This way, only the impact of the auditory cues was observed.
column2: 这样一来，被观察的就只有听觉线索的影响。

column1: The team then measured how long each type of sound held the infants’ attention.
column2: 接下来，团队测量每类声音能把婴儿的注意力吸引多久。
column4: each type of sound|每一类声音
column5: held the infants’ attention|持续吸引婴儿的注意力

column1: They found that the ‘infant’ sounds held babies’ attention nearly 40 percent longer.
column2: 他们发现，“婴儿”的声音让孩子集中注意力的时间延长了近40%。
column4: held babies’ attention|持续吸引婴儿的注意力
column5: nearly 40 percent longer|持续时间延长近40%

column1: The baby noises also induced more reactions in the listening infants, like smiling or lip moving, which approximates sound making.
column2: 婴儿的声音还让正在倾听的孩子作出更多反应，比如微笑或活动嘴唇，后者很接近发声时的动作。

column1: The team theorizes that this attraction to other infant sounds could help launch the learning process that leads to speech.
column2: 研究团队推测，婴儿对其他婴儿声音的喜爱，可能有助于启动最终使他们学会说话的学习过程。
column8: leads to speech|最终发展为说话能力

column1: ‘It may be some property of the sound that is just drawing their attention,’ says study co-author Linda Polka.
column2: “也许只是这些声音的某个特征吸引了他们的注意力。”研究合著者琳达·波尔卡说。
column4: drawing their attention|吸引他们的注意力

column1: ‘Or maybe they are really interested in that particular type of sound because they are starting to focus on their own ability to make sounds.
column2: “也许他们对这种特定的声音格外感兴趣，因为他们正开始关注自己发声的能力。
column3: particular type of sound|特定类型的声音

column1: We are speculating here but it might catch their attention because they recognize it as a sound they could possibly make.’
column2: 这只是我们的推测，但也许是因为他们听得出，那是自己也可能发出的声音，所以才会留意。”
column4: catch their attention|引起他们注意

column1: In a study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, a total of 57 babies from two slightly different age groups — seven months and eleven and a half months — were played a number of syllables from both their native language (English) and a non-native tongue (Spanish).
column2: 在《美国国家科学院院刊》发表的一项研究中，共有57名婴儿参与，分属两个年龄略有差别的组，分别为7个月和11个半月。研究人员向他们播放了若干音节，有的出自他们的母语英语，有的出自非母语西班牙语。
column3: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|《美国国家科学院院刊》
column6: eleven and a half months|十一个半月

column1: The infants were placed in a brain-activation scanner that recorded activity in a brain region known to guide the motor movements that produce speech.
column2: 研究者用脑活动扫描仪观察婴儿，记录一个特定脑区的活动。已知该区域指导发出言语所需的肌肉动作。

column1: The results suggest that listening to baby talk prompts infant brains to start practicing their language skills.
column2: 结果表明，听婴儿语会促使婴儿的大脑开始练习语言技能。

column1: ‘Finding activation in motor areas of the brain when infants are simply listening is significant, because it means the baby brain is engaged in trying to talk back right from the start, and suggests that seven-month-olds’ brains are already trying to figure out how to make the right movements that will produce words,’ says co-author Patricia Kuhl.
column2: “婴儿只是听的时候，大脑运动区就已被激活，这是个重要发现。它意味着婴儿从一开始就在尝试回应，也表明七个月大婴儿的大脑已经在试着弄清楚，该怎样作出正确的动作才能说出词语。”合著者帕特里夏·库尔说。
column8: right from the start|从一开始

column1: Another interesting finding was that while the seven-month-olds responded to all speech sounds regardless of language, the brains of the older infants worked harder at the motor activations of non-native sounds compared to native sounds.
column2: 另一项有趣的发现是，七个月大的婴儿会对所有言语声音作出反应，无论来自哪种语言；但在较大婴儿的脑内，相比母语语音，非母语语音会使运动区更加费力地活动。
column10: compared to native sounds|与母语语音相比

column1: The study may have also uncovered a process by which babies recognize differences between their native language and other tongues.
column2: 这项研究可能还揭示了婴儿辨认母语与其他语言差异的一种过程。
